Morzomotha
A miniature hexcrawl featuring
Endless stone, eternal night! Morzomotha crawls 
on and on into a bleak darkness that promises 
only death and madness. This labyrinthine abyss 
hides inhuman societies, forbidden knowledge, 
and banished gods cast down from the sunlit 
world. Few who enter here ever escape, and 
fewer still are left sound of body and mind. 
Explorers who succumb to madness become the 
nuln, lost souls left to roam the depths. Yet the 
darkness calls to some, and these adventurers 
cannot resist seeking out Morzomotha's secrets...    
See pg. 27 for Morzomotha's hex key! †Amphibious if encountered on land*New monsters, pg. 34

T
here are fools who 
say the darkness 
can be conquered.
These poets, kings, and 
philosophers gaze out over 
a bright land washed clean 
each day by the sun. They 
see beauty. Hope. Honor.
They have not walked in 
the Shadowdark. 
They have never been lost 
in a maze of gray tunnels, 
creeping along, pining for 
the warmth of a sun they 
might never see again.    
They have never held up 
a weak torch along the 
shores of a silent ocean, 
black and endless, hideous 
in its promise of death.
They have never felt the 
press of living darkness 
worming its way into their 
minds and souls, choking 
off all sanity and hope.
Know thy enemy, these 
poets and kings and 
philosophers preach.
But those who walk 
only in light have never 
truly come to know the 
darkness. 
In this fifth issue of Cursed 
Scroll Zine, we delve into 
the abominable depths 
of a subterranean region 
in the Shadowdark called 
Morzomotha!
This kingdom of lightless 
terror knows no ruler, no 
mercy, no hope.
Morzomotha cannot be 
defeated. But it can be 
mastered. Will you dare it?
Just remember the most 
important rule...
Don't drop your torch!
-Kelsey Dionne, Jan. 2026

“The endless, eternal darkness? Harmless.

-Glort, three-eyed human wyrdling

Delver Class
Steely-eyed explorers who delve 
the forgotten places of the earth. 
They always have the right tool 
or know-how to get out of a jam. 
Weapons: Club, crossbow, 
dagger, javelin, mace, shortbow, 
shortsword, spear, staff
Armor: Leather armor, 
chainmail, shields
Hit Points: 1d6 per level
Languages. You know two 
additional common languages.
Scavenger. When you expend 
the last of a consumable item 
you've carried since your last 
rest, roll a d6. On a 5 or 6, you 
regain one use of that item. 
Trailblazer. You are adept at 
exploring inhospitable, lost, 
or unknown places. You have 
advantage on the following 
tasks:
• Climbing
• Swimming
• Foraging
• Understanding unknown 
languages
• Avoiding or escaping natural 
terrain hazards
Trusty Gear. Choose one type 
of gear or weapon you can 
wield. You gain 1 + half your 
level (round down) on checks or 
attack rolls made with that type 
of gear or weapon.
2d6 Effect (reroll 10-11 if Scavenger success range is 3-6)
2 You gain 2 gear slots and an additional Trusty Gear
3-6 +1 to melee or ranged attacks and damage
7-9 +2 to Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution stat
10-11 Add one more point to your Scavenger success range
12 Choose a talent or +2 points to distribute to stats

Wyrdling Class
Those who have been called 
down into the dark, have 
listened to the gibbering of vile 
abominations, and have felt the 
rapturous presence of The Lost 
walking with them in the abyss. 
Weapons: Club, crossbow, 
dagger, pseudopod, shortbow, 
shortsword, spear
Armor: Leather armor, 
chainmail, shields
Hit Points: 1d6 per level
Languages. You know 
Primordial.
Corruption. Roll one talent on 
the Corruption Table. 
Hideous Biology. You can 
hideously stretch your body to 
fit through inch-wide cracks. 
It takes you 3 rounds to pass 
through an obstacle in this way. 
Pseudopod. You can sprout a 
clawed, horrid pseudopod from 
your body. See its details below. 
2d6 Effect
2 Gain two new Corruption talents
3-6 +2 to Strength, Dexterity, or Charisma stats
7-9 Gain a new Corruption talent
10-11 Gain +1 to attacks and damage rolls with your pseudopod

BETRAYAL
Tier 3, wizard (C)
Duration: Focus
Range: Near
One creature of LV 7 or less you 
can see in range turns on its 
allies, regarding them as hostile 
enemies for the spell's duration.
BLIGHT
Tier 1, wizard (C)
Duration: 5 rounds
Range: Self
When you cast this spell, a close-
sized patch of earth around you 
crumbles into lifeless ash.
You gain +1 to your spellcasting 
checks for the spell's duration.
DEFILE
Tier 3, wizard (C)
Duration: 5 rounds
Range: Self
When you cast this spell, a near-
sized circle of earth around you 
disintegrates into infertile ash.
For this spell's duration, treat all 
tier 1-3 spells you successfully 
cast as critical successes.
You cannot cast this spell while 
under its effects.

17
DOMINATE
Tier 4, wizard (C)
Duration: Focus
Range: Near
You subjugate the will of one 
creature of LV 9 or less that you 
can see within range.
The creature cannot act except 
to follow your commands for the 
spell's duration.
On your turn, you can command 
the creature to take actions and 
move.
The creature acts and moves 
on its turn, following any 
instructions you gave it.
ENVENOM
Tier 2, wizard (C)
Duration: Instant
Range: Close
You turn one cup or vial of 
potable liquid into a toxic poison. 
It still appears to be the original 
liquid in all ways.
A living creature of LV 10 or less 
who drinks the liquid must pass 
a DC 15 CON check or go to 0 HP. 
DISMEMBER
Tier 4, wizard (C)
Duration: Focus
Range: Near
One creature in range of LV 9 
or less loses an arm or leg (roll 
randomly to determine which). It 
takes 1d8 damage each time this 
happens.
The target loses a new limb each 
round of the spell's duration. If 
it has no other limbs to lose, it is 
instead beheaded and dies.

18
EYEBITE
Tier 1, wizard (C)
Duration: Instant
Range: Near
One creature you target takes 
1d4 damage, and it can't see you 
until the end of its next turn.
FEEBLEMIND
Tier 5, wizard (C)
Duration: 1d8 days
Range: Near
One creature of LV 10 or less 
within range has its INT and CHA 
reduced to 1 for the duration. It 
can't cast spells. 
MAZZIM'S
MESMERISM
Tier 3, wizard (C)
Duration: Focus
Range: Near
You weave a mind-numbing 
miasma of dark magic around 
your targets.
At the start of their turn, all 
humanoid creatures of LV 5 or 
less in range must pass a CHA 
check vs. the last spellcasting 
check you made. 
Creatures who fail stand 
motionless and agape, staring at 
unseen images.

19
MISCHIEF
Tier 1, wizard (C)
Duration: 5 rounds
Range: Near
You magically beguile one 
humanoid of level 2 or less 
within near range. 
The target is overcome with a 
compulsion to commit harmful 
mischief for the spell's duration. 
Each round, it tries to commit 
a sneaky, cruel act that would 
hinder or inconvenience its 
nearest ally. 
The spell ends if you or your 
allies do anything to hurt the 
target that it notices.
PHANTOMS
Tier 2, wizard (C)
Duration: Instant
Range: Near
You conjure a terrifying illusion 
that appears in the mind of one 
target of LV 3 or less in range.
The target must immediately 
make a morale check. 
PROTECTION 
FROM GOOD
Tier 1, wizard (C)
Duration: Focus
Range: Close
For the spell’s duration, lawful 
beings have disadvantage 
on attack rolls and hostile 
spellcasting checks against the 
target. These beings also can’t 
possess, compel, or beguile it.
When cast on an already-
possessed target, the possessing 
entity makes a CHA check vs. 
the last spellcasting check. On a 
failure, the entity is expelled.

20
UNLIFE
Tier 3, wizard (C)
Duration: 1 day
Range: Close
A humanoid skull you touch 
regains a semblance of its 
former life, animating with red 
witchlight in its eyes.
The skull can converse 
in Common. It retains its 
personality and memories from 
life, but its recall can be spotty if 
it's been dead a long time. 
When the spell ends, the skull 
crumbles into grave dust.
SUBJUGATE
Tier 5, wizard (C)
Duration: 1 year
Range: Close
In order to cast this spell, you 
must sprinkle a powdered 
diamond on the target. 
Choose one creature in 
range that is currently under 
the effects of a dominate, 
feeblemind, or polymorph spell 
you have cast. The duration of 
that spell becomes 1 year.
WITHER
Tier 2, wizard (C)
Duration: Instant
Range: Close
Your touch drains the life-energy 
of one target in range, dealing it 
1d6 damage.
The target takes double damage 
from the next attack or damage-
dealing spell that strikes it.
WRACK
Tier 2, wizard (C)
Duration: Focus
Range: Far
A creature you can see within 
range of LV 5 or less is overcome 
by agonizing pain.
The target must pass a CON 
check on its turn equal to your 
last spellcasting check or it 
cannot move or act.

Ball bearing. A hefty marble of 
glossy metal. On a DC 12 DEX 
check, it rolls a near distance 
along a straight line. It triggers 
traps as if it were the footfalls of 
an adult human. Once it triggers 
a trap, it is lost or destroyed.

25
Morzomotha
“This is not the sunlit world. Everything here 
lives and dies in darkness. Remember that." 
-Sid Tariniel, elf delver

26
Travel in Morzomotha
OVERVIEW
Morzomotha is a lightless 
system of caves and tunnels 
far below the surface of the 
world. Vast cathedral caves 
are as common as cramped, 
claustrophobic tunnels. 
Lightless rivers surge through 
prehistoric caverns, and even a 
black and cursed ocean crashes 
within Morzomotha's belly. 
The beings who dwell here are 
utterly alien to the surface, and 
their ways of life are anathema 
to sunborn creatures.
CLIMATE
In the depths of the earth, there 
are neither seasons nor weather. 
Instead, these deep tunnels 
are humid and cool year round, 
never changing in a way that 
drives creatures of the sun mad. 
When the season changes on 
the surface, PCs in Morzomotha 
must pass DC 12 CHA checks or 
take 1d4 CHA damage.
THE CHITTERING
Charisma damage does not heal 
as normal in Morzomotha. A 
character must be bathed in full 
sunlight for their CHA damage 
to begin healing. 
When a PC goes below 6 
CHA, The Chittering sets in. 
Their teeth begin to chatter 
uncontrollably, and they emit a 
thin, high-pitched whine that 
draws the Shadowdark's worst 
denizens like sharks to blood. 
PCs can suppress the outward 
effects of The Chittering for 1d4 
rounds with a successful DC 12 
CON check.
Characters who reach 0 CHA in 
Morzomotha go irrevocably mad.

27
010. WAILING TUNNEL
Cold wind rushes through 
this tunnel from its end point, 
creating a grating, high-pitched 
wailing (treat each rest here as 
if it has been interrupted once). 
A massive collapse blocks the 
end of the passage and creates 
a wind tunnel of air passing 
through its thin cracks. At the 
edge of the debris, a crushed 
body holds a +1 shortbow called 
Nightjar that allows the wielder 
to turn invisible for up to 3 
rounds per day (can break up).     
104. DRAINED BASIN
This bowl-like cavern is covered 
in a carpet of fish skeletons, 
petrified seaweed, and spiraling 
seashells that pop underfoot. 
The humid air still smells of long-
gone salt water. Giant crabs 
with strobing, neon eye stalks 
scavenge the seabed (3:6 chance 
encounters here are with 1d4 
giant crabs). A shattered galleon 
lies at the basin's center; here, a 
psychic giant crab (INT 18) called 
Krikmak rules as a greedy tyrant.   
111. MORZO MOTH HIVE
Curtains of opaline silk cover the 
entire rear wall of the cavern, 
punctuated by black tunnels 
where dozens of morzo moths 
nest. Six dragon-sized queens 
(LV 15, 68 HP, 3 bite +9, 3d6 + 
grab) rule over all others here, 
though their cannibalistic nature 
keeps them isolated from each 
other. Excess noise or light has 
a 2:6 chance of disturbing a 
queen, who erupts from a tunnel 
in unbridled rage. An hour of 
meticulous silk harvesting along 
the wall produces 1 pound of 
morzo moth silk worth 200 gp. 
207. THE SPIRAL
This maddening spiral confuses 
all who enter it. A navigator 
must succeed on a DC 12 INT 
check when exiting the hex or 
the party gets stuck for a day. 
At the end of the spiral's path, 
a black statue of a faceless, 
crouching figure clutches The 
Malediction Infernal (SD pg. 317). 
Touching either teleports the 
party to hex 1403.  
Morzomotha Hex Key

28
302. MIASMA
A cloud of irritating, green 
vapor spins in a broad cyclone 
around a Well of Many Worlds 
(SD pg. 321) that lies open to 
a dimension of toxic air and 
howling, translucent spirits. The 
vapor corrodes uncovered metal 
(1:6 chance per exposure that a 
metal object is destroyed).
306. THE PILLAR
An hourglass-shaped pillar of 
rock as wide as a castle rises 
from floor to distant ceiling. 40 
nuln lurk in the honeycomb of 
caves and tunnels inside it. Each 
seeks to slay the others in a 
desperate, unending game they 
call "The Trial." The nuln present 
severed heads to a being called 
Mordak that lives in the bowels 
of the pillar; it grants gifts to its 
most ruthless champions.    
407. PEARLY WENDELS
2d6 docile pearly wendels (pg. 
35) mow through a dense 
layer of pale cave moss on the 
ground. A disturbingly gleeful 
nuln named Wortim (possibly 
once a dwarf) guards them; he 
only gets upset if someone tries 
to take a wendel from the cave.
501. ESCAPE TUNNEL 
The passage angles upwards for 
miles, eventually opening to an 
area on the surface. A screaming 
cloud of 3d12 stingbats rips 
through the tunnel at the same 
time each night.
606. MOUTH OF YAO
Glazed, red stalagmites grow 
from tiny spikes into tree-like 
colossi overhead. At the center 
of this forest lies a narrow pit 
of uttermost black. A dead 
humanoid body dropped into 
this pit has a 3:6 chance of 
crawling back out possessed by 
Yao the Endless (C archmage) 
for a week. Yao is irritable, and 
most tasks are beneath his 
mighty infinitude, but he is a 
grudging ally to his summoners. 
If Yao doesn't emerge, a hostile 
rime walker does instead. 
709. THE EYES
Thousands and thousands of 
eyes are carved into the walls of 
this passage. While here, a being 
can choose to see through the 
eyes of another creature they 
name (regardless of location) in 
a brief vision. The viewer takes 
1d4 CHA damage each time.

29
802. MAD SLAVERS
A party of 15 duergar slavers 
from Maugrinhold (1601) camp 
here, using makeshift mining 
equipment to excavate into the 
cave floor. They say they have 
been summoned to free a god 
entombed in the stone, and 
they work obsessively at their 
task. They became aware of this 
summons after capturing the 
8 nuln prisoners who now toil 
in chains beside them. Perhaps 
it is all contagious madness, or 
perhaps a massive form really is 
taking shape within the rock...
810. ORACLE LAIR
A mad nest of endless, smooth 
tunnels twists through the solid 
stone. Some are sheer climbs or 
drops navigable only by flight 
or the most daring climbers. 
The walls feature circles of blue 
light that look out upon other 
subterranean locations; some 
act as two-way portals. The Ten-
Eyed Oracle drifts through this 
warren, gibbering prophecies or 
disgorging its latest "trinkets" 
into slimy piles (anything from 
junk to artifacts). The Oracle is 
the only being that can hear the 
direct thoughts of The Lost gods.  
1004. RIVER
A broad wash of translucent, 
green water surges through 
the cave. A floating island of 
rafts made of river weed, fish 
bone, and packed mud bobs 
on the tide, lashed together 
by precarious rope bridges. 50 
deep ones who call themselves 
the Thurm live among the 
rafts; they allow passage in 
exchange for living captives or 
large quantities of food. Once 
a year, the Thurm descend the 
Abyss (1005) on treacherous rope 
ladders to leave live sacrifices at 
the threshold of the ziggurat. 
1005. THE ABYSS
A thundering waterfall blasts 
out over the edge of a broad 
sinkhole filled with hazy mist. 
500 feet below, the shallow 
water laps sluggishly around 
a three-tiered, basalt ziggurat 
crusted with trilobite fossils. 
Reclusive brain eaters dwell 
within and worship the Nautiloid 
Mother, an antediluvian goddess 
from time before time. They 
offer living humanoids to the 
goddess for "evolution." A rare 
few survive this grotesque ritual 
and transform into brain eaters.

30
1010. OFFERING STATUES
Six leering, bat-faced statues 
(gargoyles) perch at the point 
where the tunnel splits into 
two major arteries. Clay bowls 
of dried blood, bound skeletal 
remains, and four rubies (200 gp 
each) lie at their feet. An offering 
of living flesh or 200 gp sates the 
gargoyles, allowing safe passage.   
1105. GRIZZENGHAST
A lightless city rises above the 
Abyss (1005), clinging to its 
precipice like a roosting harpy. 
Its stone towers snake drunkenly 
upward, twisted and precarious, 
lashed together by cords of 
morzo moth silk. Here, 3,000 
gray-skinned fiends called the 
dremir make their home. The 
streets are wet and serpentine, 
and a grim quiet prevails, for the 
eyeless dremir are sensitive to 
noise and flame. They silently 
crowd visitors, grinning painfully, 
but always keeping at arm's 
length as required by their laws. 
They are a people wealthy in 
sorcerous knowledge, crafting, 
and culture. A visitor is safe for 
three days total in a month; 
the moment this expires, the 
ravenous dremir fall upon them.    
1109. NIGHTBOUND SEA
Churning waves break against 
the black pebble beach of this 
underground sea. The reek 
of algae and decay boils off 
its surface. Monolithic basalt 
pillars thrust from the foul 
water like towers, each carved 
with spiraling glyphs. Deep 
below the surface, one of The 
Lost gods rests on the seafloor, 
bound in ever-burning chains 
forged by Madeera and Memnon 
together in their only act of 
unity. Wretched aboleths and 
aquatic brain eaters attend to 
this titanic god as it lies in silent 
repose, neither dead nor alive.
1202. RALK'S CHIMNEY
A faint, gray glow at the top 
of this vast cavern hints at an 
exit to the sunlit surface. This 
miles-long, narrowing chimney 
is named after the legendary 
thief Ralk, the only person to 
ever survive its treacherous 
climb. Scaling the chimney takes 
four days and requires pinning 
oneself to the wall to sleep, 
often alongside the rope-bound 
corpses of other failed climbers. 
Giant spiders and morzo moths 
nest all along its perilous walls.

31
1403. MEDUSA DEN
Odd clusters of stalagmites are 
actually petrified humanoids 
and beasts that have been 
artfully posed by Kalithia, a

Overview
BACKGROUND
Nobody knows where the grinning Librarians of Leng came from. 
These creatures might be demons, or they might even be living 
manifestations of the Shadowdark's madness. They have dwelt in 
the Library since time long forgotten, deep in the darkness, never to 
be seen by mankind. There, they catalogue the nightmares, terrors, 
and fears that flow through this dimension. The Librarians of Leng 
know a crucial fact about every being who has walked this world: 
what they fear most. To some, there is no greater treasure.  
FACTIONS
Librarians of Leng. Masters of the Library. Keepers of the deep lore. 
These blindfolded beings stalk in silk robes through ancient halls. 
Captive deep ones, trolls, and gargoyles serve them. Horrid grins 
twist their faces; they can make no other expression than painful joy.
Prisoners. Trespassers, deep delvers, and wizards who teleported to 
the wrong place. The Librarians lock up any intruders so their fears 
can be provoked and studied. Prisoners who still cling to sanity are 
united in their desire to escape, setting all else aside.
Books. Some sentient books do not want to be housed in the 
Library of Leng, so they seek a way out. Many are self-serving and 
will only keep alliances for as long as they are convenient. Others are 
noble and wish their knowledge to be returned to the world.

THE LIBRARY OF LENG
The Library of Leng is a castle of green-black rock that stretches 
into windowless, pointed spires as if shaped from clay. High-relief 
carvings of colossal figures spring out of its walls, each as tall as 
the castle itself. They depict tentacled and winged horrors locked 
in mortal combat with thrashing dragons. The entire structure sits 
heavily on a pillar of stone surrounded by a 200'-deep ravine. A thin, 
arching bridge dripping with strands of fungi crosses this expanse; 
it deposits visitors at a tunnel mouth leading into the castle's base.
ORDER OF BATTLE
Intelligent creatures (excluding sentient books) in adjacent rooms 
investigate unusual sounds, arriving in 1d4 rounds. A Librarian of 
Leng whose morale breaks retreats toward Area 52 to release the 
bezelak. If it succeeds, all random encounters have a 3:6 chance of 
being with the bezelak for the next day. During this time, checks 
to sneak and hide are DC 18 and encounters with the Librarians of 
Leng or their servants are always hostile.
ENTRANCES AND EXITS
Area 1. A bridge crosses over the ravine and into a tunnel mouth at 
the base of the Library. This tunnel leads to Area 1.
Area 12. An overflow grate in the cistern (Area 12) covers a chute 
that exits the pillar of rock 60 feet below the Library. Crusted lichen 
and white, chalky minerals surround the mouth of it. PCs can climb 
between it and the bridge to Area 1 with two DC 15 STR/DEX checks. 
Area 15. A wagon-sized carving of a beast with 10 snaking eyestalks 
and a crescent moon maw (The Ten-Eyed Oracle) lurks at the rear 
side of the Library above a narrow precipice of rock. It seems out of 
proportion to the rest of the gigantic figures surrounding it. A secret 
door built into this beast's scarred central eye opens to Area 15.

• Pillars. Touching a pillar allows one to view the nightmares of the 
victim on the altar (see below) as if through their eyes.
• Altar. Oily black marble placed on an ornamental red carpet. A 
creature lain upon the altar enters an endless nightmare (DC 15 
CHA to resist) until it is removed. 
 ▶ Carpet. A Flying Carpet (SD pg. 303). The weighty altar requires 
a DC 20 STR check to lift for long enough to pull it free. 
• Woman. A powerful young witch, Anamaxis (C archmage). Proud 
and cold. She is currently without spells and suffering from 
extreme deprivation. Her priority is escaping the Library of Leng.
28. EYE OF DEATH
Patches of black powder are sprinkled on the floor. The northeast 
wall has a broad, oval-shaped carving at it center. 
• Locked Door. DC 20 DEX/18 STR to open.
• Powder. Smells of charred meat (it's disintegrated bodies).
• Carving. A closed eye. It opens when any creature in the 
room speaks in a language other than Primordial. It shoots a 
disintegration ray at the offender (DC 15 DEX or 5d8 damage).

51
Level 2: Areas 29-64
d6 Details
1 2d4 Librarians of Leng taking a mage prisoner to Area 52
2 6 deep ones leading a trained frost troll on a collar and chain
3 2 Librarians of Leng arguing about who misplaced a book

5 A lone deep one drunk on morzo moth milk from Area 37
6 The Ten-Eyed Oracle departing after delivering a prophecy
RANDOM ENCOUNTERS
Danger Level. Risky. Check for an encounter every 2 rounds.
Light. Total darkness unless otherwise noted.
29. ENTRY TUNNEL
Two grand doors of engraved, black-green stone tower overhead 
in the east passage. A thick gate of iron bars blocks a tunnel to the 
south. To the far west, the air shimmers like a mirage.
• Doors. 15' high. Carvings of thrashing, intertwined eel-snakes hide 
two subtle hand imprints at 6' in height. Pushing the doors open 
with a hand in each imprint prevents its trap from activating. 
 ▶ Trap. All creatures within near are outlined in a sickly green 
aura of light for 10 rounds. For affected creatures, all spells are 
DC 15 to cast and they cannot knowingly utter a lie.
• Gate. DC 20 STR to lift. Lever to operate it in Area 45. Four captive 
frost trolls lurk in Area 46 and sometimes beg and threaten 
passersby in broken Giant for their release.
• Mirage. Teleports creatures who walk through it to Area 14.

52
30. JADE HALL
A vast, silent hall reaches up and out into endless darkness. Jade 
floor tiles flare with a reflective glow as light washes over them. 
• Hidden Watchposts. Areas 31 and 56 overlook the hall through 
hidden arrow slits (can be found by actively looking). A Librarian 
of Leng watches from inside each. 
 ▶ Hostile. Librarians immediately attack any creatures outlined in 
the green aura from the door trap in Area 29.
• Lever. On the wall outside the door to Area 52. It opens and closes 
the grate covering the pit in Area 52.
31. HIDDEN WATCHPOST
A tall, purple-skinned being in red robes presses its silk-wrapped 
face up against arrow slits lining the walls. It sniffs at the air.
• Being. A Librarian of Leng monitors Area 30 through arrow slits 
hidden from the outside.
 ▶ Hostile. Librarian immediately attacks any creatures outlined in 
the green aura from the door trap in Area 29.
• Secret Door. To Area 33.
32. FORTUNE-TELLER
A goblin in a silk turban sits on a pillow inside a tall glass cube on a 
red base. Dazzling lights along the glass flash in wavelike patterns.
• Goblin. The Great Zambini, a mechanical goblin. He tells a fortune 
with strobing eyes and a robotic voice when 1 gp is inserted into 
a vertical slot in the cube's base. Anyone who inserts more than 5 
gp a day: DC 15 CON check or struck deaf and blind for one day.
 ▶ Fortunes. Roll 1d6. 1: Misfortune. A random item you carry 
disappears forever. 2: Woe. Lose 1d6 XP. 3: Unclear. Lose a luck 
token. 4: Promising. Gain a luck token. 5: Weal. Gain 1d4 XP. 6: 
Good fortune. A weapon you carry gains a permanent +1 bonus.

53
33. BOOKS OF DRAGONS
Black mahogany bookshelves reach to the ceiling. They house a few 
hundred tomes bound in pebbled reptile skin of jewel-toned colors. 
• Tomes.  Each closely details the life of every dragon that has ever 
lived. It takes 4 rounds to find a specific dragon by name.
 ▶ Reading. Books are in Draconic. 3:6 chance that opening one 
unleashes a dragon breath weapon at the opener matching the 
book's coloration. Reading at least 3 tomes grants the reader a 
permanent boon of fireblood, frostblood, or stormblood (once 
per reader, see dragon talents, SD pg. 210-211).
 ▶ Draconification. Stealing a book causes the thief to gradually 
turn into a wyvern over 2d6 days (reverses if book is returned).
• Secret Door. To Area 31.
34. BOOKS OF MORTALS
A dense forest of teetering, stacked books spirals toward the ceiling. 
The books are a wild mess of different colors, shapes, and materials. 
• Books. Each is a log of the fears of every member of a mortal 
family line (all ancestries). Finding a specific book takes 4 hours 
without a Librarian of Leng, who can find any title instantly.
 ▶ Reading. Tomes are in the relevant ancestry's language. Several 
books have purple ink blotting out entries; this ink (from Area 
59) can erase a fear from the book, erasing it in real life as well.
35. CHECKOUT DESK
A 9-foot tall, purple-skinned being in yellow silk robes slumps at a 
stone desk with his hand on his chin, tapping his fingers.
• Being. A young and bored Librarian of Leng named Terkule on 
checkout desk duty. Has a one-sided grudge against Cirroc (Area 
61) over a forgotten insult and wants to see him humiliated.
• Desk. Cluttered with books. Bottle of Magic Ink (SD pg. 306).

54
36. CURIO MUSEUM
Dozens of orderly wall niches each display a unique trinket.
• Trinkets. Most are worthless novelties from the surface world. 
Plaques describe each object and its "far-flung" origin. Tea cup, 
magnifying glass, pinned butterfly, demon mask, horse shoe, etc.   
 ▶ Blue Cube. 4 inches wide, metallic. Touching it to a living 
creature allows wielder to transform into that creature for up to 
10 rounds a day. Cube can hold one memorized transformation 
at a time; wielder can change it to a new creature.   
37. REFRESHMENTS CHAMBER
A lone imp wearing a blue velvet tailcoat sits in the middle of a long 
dining table and saws tunelessly on a viol. Trays of dainty appetizers 
and silver ewers full of dark liquids surround him.
• Imp.  Smellik, a burdensome "gift" from a visiting demon prince. 
The Librarians of Leng don't know what to do with him and have 
DISADV on spellcasting while he's playing viol within earshot.
• Appetizers. Crab cakes, aboleth roe, seared cave slug. All slimy. 
• Ewers. Morzo moth milk. DC 12 CON per gulp or drunk 10 rounds.
38. BOOKS OF DEMONS
Black shelves are crammed with tomes bound in crudely stitched 
skins, sheets of metal, or oily leathers. Room reeks of sulfur.
• Tomes.  Written in Diabolic and sorted randomly. Each is a first-
person autobiography from the perspective of a demon; it 
updates even while being read. Finding a specific book takes 2 
hours (a Librarian of Leng can find any title instantly).
 ▶ Mirror-Bound Tome. The Princess of the Ivory Palace, Yarina 
Tesura, is trapped inside a book with a mirrored cover. The 
pages narrate as a demon relentlessly chases her. The only way 
to free her is by writing a new sentence into the book narrating 
her escape with the Purple Ink from Area 59.

55
39. SORTING ROOM
A muttering, long-limbed being in green silk robes trudges around 
depositing books onto wheeled carts.
• Being. A Librarian of Leng named Hakiri. On sorting duty as 
punishment after trying to tame a stingbat (wants one as a pet).
• Carts. Ordinary books mixed with 2 sentient books who want to 
escape the Library. They whisper entreaties to potential allies.
 ▶ "Dimensional Tunneling" (nerdy about space-time; contains 
a Spell Scroll of Dimension Door), "Training Trolls" (strict and 
disciplined; all trolls have DISADV to attack the book's wielder).
40. BOOKS OF ANGELS
Marble columns and stained glass panels form bookshelves that 
hold glittering ivory tomes. A note is pinned near the door.
• Tomes.  Alabaster and mother-of-pearl bindings. Illuminated 
manuscripts in Celestial. Each details the holy deeds of an angel. 
Perfect organization allows any book to be found in 5 rounds. 
• Note. "To all scholars: Research indicates angels do not harbor 
inborn fears. Headmaster Xenoxes will purchase a captured angel 
(1,000 gp) to subject to fear-inculcation experiments."
41. BLACK ORB
In this chilly, silent room, a statue of a 15-foot tall Librarian of Leng 
holds out a clawed hand; a black orb hovers over its open palm.
• Trap. Trying to open any door into Area 41 without wearing the 
Talisman of Leng (Area 59) teleports the being to Area 50.
• Orb. A 3-foot wide Sphere of Annihilation (SD pg. 315). Librarians 
of Leng have ADV on INT checks to move it.
• Statue. If anyone tries to move the Sphere, the statue vies for 
control of it (+4 INT bonus and ADV) and targets PCs. It can not 
control the Sphere once the orb moves outside of Area 41.

56
42. BOOKS OF PRIMORDIALS
Black, bent statuettes of winged and tentacled abominations crowd 
the wall shelves. The ceiling extends up and up into darkness. Light 
can't fully banish the shadows that spread like pools of oil.
• Ceiling. Stretches infinitely up with row after row of statuettes.
• Statuettes. Dull black stone, 2 feet high, each a different 
primordial being. Every statuette holds the book that describes 
the members of its species. Finding a specific book takes 3 hours 
and requires flight (a Librarian of Leng can locate it immediately).
 ▶ "The Hexagonal Tome." Held by the brain eater statuette. The 
visiting brain eaters in Area 11 want to steal it.
 ▶ "Servants of the Eye." Held by the Librarian of Leng statuette. 
Every Librarian of Leng instantly becomes aware if someone 
touches the book. They savagely pursue anyone who does so.
43. THE BOOK OF IMMORTALS
An infinitely black room that echoes cavernously. A beam of light in 
the far distance pours down onto a marble plinth holding a book.
• Book. An ordinary, brown leather tome titled "That Which 
Is." Each chapter is infinite in length and describes a unique 
immortal being. It can't be removed from its plinth.
 ▶ Reading. A mortal who reads passages about their god or 
patron gains a patron boon or class talent (once only). Reading 
about an immortal whose alignment does not match the 
reader's requires a DC 15 CHA check or the reader goes mad.
44. SILENT READING ROOM
Oversized, plush armchairs cluster around the edges of the room.  
• Armchairs. All sound is muted for anyone sitting in one.
 ▶ Book. "An Analysis of Mirror Demons," left open on the seat of 
an armchair. Contains a Spell Scroll of Mirror Image.

57
45. TROLL TRAINING GEAR
Wall racks hold coiled black whips, iron neck collars big enough for 
bears, and iron chains. A lever protrudes from the northeast wall.
• Locked Door. DC 20 DEX/18 STR to open.
• Trap. A hair-thin tripwire crosses each threshold to the north, 
west, and south, causing a hidden bucket of caustic acid (3d6 
damage) to fall on anyone in the threshold (DC 15 DEX to avoid).  
• Racks. One hook cradles a +2 whip called Backbiter. 1/day, on a 
missed attack with it, turn the miss into a critical hit instead. Any 
frost troll that sees Backbiter must make a morale check.
 ▶ Whip. Melee weapon, near range, 1d4 damage, finesse property.
• Lever. Ordinary iron. Operates gate leading into Area 29.
46. FROST TROLL CAVE
Four rangy giants with warty blue skin and black eyes pace 
restlessly at the end of thick chains bolted around their necks.  
• Giants. 4 frost troll captives. They whine, plead, and threaten 
to be released in broken Giant. Trolls: Sibolg (ringleader), Erdak 
(aggressive), Mulda (devious), Bral (cowardly). 
 ▶ Neck Chains. 10' long, bolted to wall. DC 20 STR to break. Freed 
trolls betray all agreements and run to Area 47 to massacre the 
trainer. Then they go on a wild rampage. Random encounters 
have a 3:6 chance of being with the trolls until they are killed. 
47. TROLL TRAINER
A rotund, fish-faced man sits at a low table and gobbles a steaming 
plate of crab with both hands, flinging bits of it everywhere.
• Locked Door. DC 20 DEX/18 STR to open.
• Man. Troll trainer. A flatulent and overconfident deep one named 
Urghast. Feels other deep ones are beneath him and would like 
to see them "put in their place." Has a key to Areas 45 and 47.

58
48. MESS HALL
Two fish-faced men sit alone at tables and shovel plates of food into 
their slobbering, fanged mouths. They shoot glares at each other.
• Men. Two deep ones, Borbin (hot-headed, sarcastic) and Mulko 
(irritable, greedy). Each believes the other cheated on a recent 
dice game. A shouting match erupts between them in 2 rounds, 
and a fist fight 2 rounds after that.
 ▶ Rematch. Both would agree to a rematch to settle the dispute.
 ▶ Treasure. Mulko quaffs a stolen Potion of Giant Strength before 
pummeling Borbin. Otherwise, he tries to pawn it off to the PCs. 
49. DEEP ONES QUARTERS
Shallow pools of lapping water pockmark the floor. Human-like 
shapes float inside them. The smell of fish is overwhelming.
• Pools. Waist-deep, the size of a human bed. 6 deep ones float on 
them face-down, asleep. DC 12 DEX to sneak by them unnoticed.
 ▶ Treasure. A sleeping deep one wears a waterlogged Bag of 
Holding (SD pg. 299) on his belt filled with 300 pounds of 
slightly off fish. DC 15 DEX to pluck it free without waking him. 
• Key. A master key to all locked areas hangs by the east door.
50. MASSACRE CAVE
Piles of bones and dried gore carpet the cave floor in a sticky mess. 
Heavy snuffling and scraping echoes from the north.
• Bezelak. For each loud noise, cumulative 1:6 chance the bezelak 
in Area 51 comes to investigate. 
• Treasure. A gold and ruby glint on a mangled skeleton's hand is a 
Ring of Fireballs (SD pg. 312). 
• Bars. Heavy iron. Blocks the west passage. DC 20 STR to lift.
• Secret Door. In the rock pillar. It opens to a slippery, corkscrewing 
tunnel that climbs 60' (DC 18 DEX to climb) and exits into Area 8.

59
51. BEZELAK LAIR
A broad cave tunnel. Black streaks of feces and blood paint every 
surface. Overhead, a square shaft reaches up to a distant grate. The 
eye-watering stench of algae and sulfur boils thickly in the air. 
• Bezelak. Clings to the wall 20' up, camouflaged by the muck-
spattered stone (it gets a surprise round if unnoticed). It's very 
hungry and does not discriminate between friend or foe.
• Shaft. 40' high. Covered in a heavy grate. Leads to Area 52.
52. DROP PIT
A narrow walkway surrounds a grate-covered pit dropping into 
darkness. The reek of sulfur and stagnant water wafts through it.
• Locked Door. DC 20 DEX/18 STR to open.
• Pit. Covered in a grate (lever to withdraw it is outside door in Area 
30). The bezelak in Area 51 can swiftly climb the pit's 40' walls.
53. OBSERVATION CAVE
A high platform thrusts out over a dripping cave strewn with bones.
• Platform. 40' high, leads to Area 54. The underside is greased 
regularly with tallow (pg. 22), making it too slippery to climb.
• Man. A gap-toothed old man (peasant) who calls himself Prince 
Rork lurks in the shadows. He wears stitched-together skins 
and alternates between a tittering stream-of-consciousness and 
wheezing laughter. The bezelak (Area 51) refuses to eat him. 
 ▶ Caw. If in danger, he screeches a hawk-like caw, instantly 
summoning the bezelak from Area 51.
 ▶ Treasure. He wears hidden stacks of jewelry under his tunic and 
trades them for food. 1. Hefty gold and mithral braid (200 gp), 
2. Gold snake cuff with emerald eyes, as Bracers of Archery (SD 
pg. 301) 3. White gold chain with cat-eye ruby (250 gp), 4. Silver 
and pearl torc (150 gp), 5. Half-moon sapphire pendant (300 gp).

60
54. PRISONERS
Two dark shapes crouch inside a heavily barred prison cell. Quiet 
whimpers and the occasional hysterical shriek erupt from within.
• Locked Doors. DC 20 DEX/18 STR to open.
• Prison Cell. Holds subjects of the Librarians' torturous research.
 ▶ Angel. An unarmored, weaponless archangel named Apolion. 
His wings are shorn and crudely stitched (can move near). 
Experimental fear conditioning has at last broken him; he is 
madly terrified of beetles and believes they are everywhere. 
 ▶ Gorilla. An intelligent gorilla named Tektumi (pragmatic and 
long-suffering, ruefully accepts his fate). He is wary friends with 
Apolion and contemplates putting the angel out of his misery.
• Curtain. Leads to an observation platform 40' high over the cave 
in Area 53. The underside of the platform is greased regularly with 
tallow (pg. 22), making it too slippery to climb.
55. TIME DILATION ZONE
The air trembles with a subtly disorienting motion. Flickering 
shadows stutter and sometimes reverse their movement. 
• Time Instability. Passing through this area causes all timed 
effects (including torches) to randomly reset to a new duration.
• Secret Door. In southeastern hallway. Goes to Area 56.
56. HIDDEN WATCHPOST
A lanky, purple-skinned being in blue robes holds its silk-wrapped 
head against the arrow slits along the walls, listening intently.
• Being. A Librarian of Leng monitors Area 30 through arrow slits 
hidden from the outside.
 ▶ Hostile. Librarian immediately attacks any creatures outlined in 
the green aura from the door trap in Area 29.
• Secret Door. To southeastern hallway of Area 55.

61
57. WATER ILLUSION
Translucent green water fills this room from top to bottom, cutting 
off abruptly at the open threshold to the east. 
• Illusion. Each time entering, DC 15 INT or perceive the room to be 
filled with salt water. "Swim" at half speed. Can actually drown.
58. ELITE GUARDS
Two men in black, spiny plate armor and helms stand at attention. 
The southeast wall has a broad, oval-shaped carving at it center. 
• Men. Elite deep one guards (treat as reavers with the deep one's 
sunblind trait). Nobody except Librarians of Leng may pass; they 
demand explanations in Primordial.
• Carving. A closed eye. It opens when any creature in the 
room speaks in a language other than Primordial. It shoots a 
disintegration ray at the offender (DC 15 DEX or 5d8 damage). 
59. HEAD LIBRARIAN'S OFFICE
A towering being in purple robes with intricate gold trim sits at a 
desk and passes its fingers over the open page of a book, mouthing 
words to itself with a hideous grin.
• Locked Door. DC 20 DEX/18 STR to open.
• Being. The head Librarian of Leng, Xenoxes. Ruthless, precise. 
Fascinated with the common fears of surface-dwellers, such as 
spiders, snakes, and darkness. Wishes to study these trends.
 ▶ Treasure. Has a master key to all locked areas and wears the 
Talisman of Leng, a mithral pendant with a clawed hand 
clutching a black pearl with a silver snake-eye pupil. Its wielder 
gains +2 AC and can summon The Ten-Eyed Oracle as an ally 
for 10 rounds once a month (the Oracle hates overuse of this).
• Desk. 3 vials of Purple Ink (each enough for a short sentence). Ink 
can alter entries in any of the books in Areas 33, 34, 38, 40, and 42. 
It does not work on the Books of Immortals in Area 43.

62
60. COMMUNING CHAMBER
A monumental stone archway carved with gargoyles and a leering 
demon face fills the west wall. Moss and fungi spirals up its pillars. 
On the east wall, an oily green tome stands inside an alcove.  
• Archway. Large enough for an elephant. Between the arches, a 
surface of inky darkness ripples like water and absorbs all light.
 ▶ Surface. Touching it reveals a distant, silent image of The Ten-
Eyed Oracle. The Oracle turns and approaches the viewer, 
crossing through the archway into Area 60 in 1d4 rounds unless 
someone touches the surface again, deactivating the archway.
• Tome.  The Tome of Leng. Bound in basilisk skin. A snake-like 
eye rolls around on the cover. Each time a mortal being opens 
the book, they age 2d6 years. A random sorcerer spell (pg. 15) 
appears inside the book each time it's opened.
61. SCRIBING HALL
Four lavender-skinned, willowy beings with pained smiles hunch 
over writing desks and scratch black quills across parchment. 
• Beings. 4 Librarians of Leng named Cirroc (irritable), Medzel 
(overwhelmed), Jalash (languid), and Vireen (fussy).
• Desks. Carefully stacked piles of scribed parchment. Scattering 
the piles causes the Librarians to sink helplessly to their knees in 
mental agony for one round. 
62. BOOK BINDING HALL
Two silk-robed, purple beings with mocking grins carefully pull 
needles and thread through stacks of parchment. Partially bound 
books crowd the work tables.
• Beings. 2 Librarians of Leng named Darog (cool-headed) and 
Nuriok (gossipy).
• Books. The only complete tome is "The Red Spectacle," a tale of 
gladiatorial prowess (reader gains +1 to melee attacks, one use).

63
63. DISTANT PORTALS
Translucent ovals lined in blue light float inside each alcove.
• Ovals. Portals to far-flung locations. They exit to remote areas: 
a lush tropical jungle, a glaringly bright desert, a mist-choked 
forest, a pebble beach dusted in snow, and a vast cathedral cave.    
 ▶ Return. The portals disappear behind users unless a person 
crossing through wears the Talisman of Leng (Area 59).
64. WENDEL STABLES
Two cow-sized slugs with spiny carapaces trawl the room, slurping 
up bloody piles of chopped meat. They wear riding saddles.
• Wendels. Two spiny wendels trained for Librarian of Leng riders. 
DC 15 CHA for others to ride (recheck each time wendel is under 
duress or startled). On a failure, the wendel attacks the rider.
 ▶ Lil' Sweetie. Friendly, food-motivated, hideously cute.
 ▶ Baylight. Scintillating brown hide, skeptical, hates deep ones.
